preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 5 and 200,000 inclusive.
There are exactly n-1 edges describing the tree structure.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct valid cities within the range [1, n].
The number of test cases t is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and 1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and u != v and x != y for u, v, x, y in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query contains four distinct valid cities where the start and end points for each runner are distinct.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, str) and (line == '-1' or line.isdigit()) for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is either the string '-1' or a non-negative integer string representing minutes.

postconditions.expression: all((int(output_lines[i]) == 0) == (queries[i][0] == queries[i][2]) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: If the runners start at the same city (u == x), the output is 0; otherwise, it is non-zero (unless they meet immediately at t=0 which implies u=x).

postconditions.expression: all((int(output_lines[i]) == -1) == (not exists_meeting_time(queries[i], tree_adj)) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: The output is -1 if and only if the two runners never meet at the same city at the same integer time step.

postconditions.expression: all((int(output_lines[i]) != -1) == (min_meeting_time(queries[i], tree_adj) == int(output_lines[i])) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: If a meeting occurs, the output is the minimum non-negative integer time t such that the position of runner JH at time t equals the position of runner JY at time t.
